Unauthenticated like `/open`, and for the same kind of reason: the answer

With `q` the answer comes from fuzzy matching, so "matan" and "матан" both
work. Without it, one level of the tree is returned.

A couple of hundred rows — cheaper to send once than to paginate, and the

post.description:
Read a sentence and show back what we made of it.

Every call is logged with its parse and result count. Queries that match
nothing are the ranked list of what the catalog is missing, and the raw
text next to the parse is what a better parser would be trained on.

Record that someone is about to write, and hand back the link.

The conversation itself happens in Telegram, where both people already are.
What we keep is that it started — which is the only honest basis for the
response times and deal counts shown on a card. Self-reported numbers would
be worth nothing.

get.description:
Read back the caller's own profile, whatever state it is in.

Answers with an empty shell rather than 404 when there is no profile yet:
the screen behind this is a form, and a form that has to branch on a
missing-resource error to decide whether to render is a form with two
code paths where one will do.

AlsoSubject.description: A subject the parser guessed at but would not search by.

Avatar.title: Avatar
Avatar.description:
Enough to draw the little circle without fetching anything.

Telegram avatar URLs expire, so a monogram is the fallback rather than a
broken image. The colour is derived from the user id, which keeps the same
person the same colour across screens.

Chip.title: Chip
Chip.description: One piece of what we understood, shown back for correction.

Clarify.title: Clarify
Clarify.description:
One question, asked only when the answer changes the result set.

Never a wall of filters — if we cannot justify asking, we do not ask.

FeedRequestOut.title: FeedRequestOut
FeedRequestOut.description:
A request as a helper sees it.

Deliberately not a subclass of RequestOut: how many people have already
answered, and who they are, is the competition's business and not this
reader's. A helper who can see "3 answers already" simply skips those,
which is the opposite of what the feed is for — and inheriting the fields
to blank them would still leave them in the schema.

HelperCardOut.title: HelperCardOut
HelperCardOut.description: One row in the results list.

MyHelperOut.title: MyHelperOut
MyHelperOut.description:
The caller's own profile, draft or hidden included.

`/helpers/{id}` deliberately refuses anything unpublished, which is
correct for the catalog and leaves someone with a draft unable to read
back what they wrote. This is the other door.

MyOfferOut.title: MyOfferOut
MyOfferOut.description:
One row of the caller's own offers, ready to be edited and sent back.

Both the id and the name of every axis: the id is what `HelperUpsert`
wants, the name is what the person reads. `OfferOut` carries only the
names, which is right for a card and useless for a form.

Phrase.title: Phrase
Phrase.description:
A sentence for the client to render, not a sentence.

`{"code": "reason.same_exam", "params": {"taught": 40, "passed": 38}}`
becomes "Готовил к этому же экзамену 40 человек, сдали 38" — with correct
plural agreement, which only the client can produce.

PlacementSlot.title: PlacementSlot
PlacementSlot.description: Where a partner block may appear. Grows as screens are added.

RequestOut.title: RequestOut
RequestOut.description: Your own request. Who answered is the whole point of the screen.

ServiceForm.title: ServiceForm
ServiceForm.description:
The shape of the form that offers a kind of help.

A different question from ``ServiceGroup``, and deliberately a separate
column. The group is for the student browsing — *what do I need*. The shape
is for the person offering — *what do we ask you*. They nearly coincide, and
the places they do not are the ones that matter: help *during* an exam sits
on the entrance shelf, where a student compares it with exam preparation,
and its form has nothing to do with teaching.

``work`` is always remote, so its form does not ask how you work. Lessons
and errands ask the same three answers under different words; see
docs/data-model.md.

ServiceGroup.title: ServiceGroup
ServiceGroup.description:
Which shelf a kind of help sits on.

Both screens that show these tiles — the catalog's front door and the
screen where someone offers a service — render the same list grouped by
this. ``life`` is the help that has no subject and no institution: the
paperwork of staying in the country rather than of studying.

Closed on purpose. Group names are translated on the client, the way
``work_format`` and ``price_unit`` are; see docs/data-model.md.

ServiceOptionOut.title: ServiceOptionOut
ServiceOptionOut.description: One line of what a kind of help covers, in the caller's language.

UiLang.title: UiLang
UiLang.description:
Interface languages.

Separate from the languages people teach in — there can be more of those.
Note the standard codes: the legacy bot used ``cz``/``ua``, which have to be
mapped to ``cs``/``uk`` during the data import.
